paths.description: Landing portal and game discovery entry point; tests primary navigation, preferences, privacy interruption and global performance.
Dota 2 wiki main page, representing game-level landing and category navigation.
Tournament detail template, representing event schedules and dense tabular content.
Team profile template, representing long-form entity pages.
Search journey from query to exact team result; represents the primary find-content flow.
Missing wiki page state, representing recovery from an unavailable result.

findings.summary: Consent wall obscures the primary content on every fresh visit
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots across all five representative templates show a large fixed consent panel covering roughly half the viewport before any interaction. On mobile it masks the event/team content while presenting 1,192 vendors.
findings.suggestedFix: Delay non-essential consent UI until needed, keep core content unobscured, and provide an immediate light-dismiss or equally direct continue-with-essential-only action.

findings.summary: The consent wall is not exposed as a dialog
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found zero dialog, role=dialog, or aria-modal elements while screenshots show a modal-like overlay; focus and dismissal therefore rely on third-party ad-hoc markup.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement the flow with a native dialog (or equivalent correctly labelled modal semantics), focus containment, Escape handling, and focus restoration.

findings.summary: No explicit high-contrast preference adaptation was found
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found prefers-color-scheme but no prefers-contrast handling; the prefers-contrast screenshot was pixel-identical in size to the default capture.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast rules for controls, borders, links, focus indicators, and custom scrollbars without suppressing system colors.

findings.summary: Reusable cards adapt only at the page/viewport level
findings.evidence: Rendered CSS inspection found no @container or container-type despite reusable wiki cards appearing in multiple widths. Mobile reflow works, but components are coupled to viewport breakpoints.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare containment on reusable card regions and use size container queries for card density, labels, and controls while retaining a fallback.

findings.summary: Throttled mobile load misses the LCP and responsiveness bar
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 4.4 s, TBT 1,100 ms, max potential FID 820 ms, and time-to-interactive 23.9 s (performance score 0.53). The first-party trace was faster but still recorded 165 ms TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP request chain, prioritise the LCP asset, and defer non-critical ad/analytics work until after content and interaction readiness.

findings.summary: Third-party and application scripts block the main thread
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported 3.5 s main-thread work and 2.2 s JavaScript execution. The trace found a 215 ms long task and mobile layouts repeatedly observed roughly 220 ms tasks.
findings.suggestedFix: Break application work into yielding tasks and load advertising, replay analytics, and bidder code conditionally after interaction or idle.

findings.summary: Resource delivery has avoidable cache and render-path costs
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 119 requests and 3.51 MB transferred; ten first-party CSS/JS/font resources lacked useful cache headers. Lighthouse estimated 1,027 KiB cache savings and 450 ms render-blocking savings. DOM confirmation shows index.js is a deferred-by-spec module, but three stylesheets remain parser-blocking.
findings.suggestedFix: Set long immutable caching on versioned assets, inline only critical CSS, defer non-critical styles, and preserve module/defer loading for scripts.

findings.summary: The page ships a large amount of unused and third-party JavaScript
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 1,160 KiB unused JavaScript and 54 KiB unused CSS. HAR attributes 2.50 MB to 40 scripts, with 2.53 MB of all transfer bytes from third parties.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split the landing experience and remove, deduplicate, or interaction-gate ad, analytics, session-replay, and legacy bundles.

findings.summary: Some inline links rely on colour alone
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility found two text-block links distinguished from surrounding text only by colour, despite an otherwise strong 0.96 accessibility score.
findings.suggestedFix: Add an underline or another non-colour cue in the default and hover/focus states, preserving sufficient contrast in both themes.

findings.summary: Browser errors are emitted during load
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed the errors-in-console audit on the landing page. HAR also recorded a missing commons.jpg and aborted third-party requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the broken asset reference and address first-party console exceptions; isolate third-party failures so they do not pollute the application error channel.

findings.summary: Asset and platform diagnostics are not clean
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported a deprecated API and a low-resolution image; HAR returned 404 for /static/images/wikis/commons.jpg. The document itself has valid HTML doctype and UTF-8 charset.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the deprecated API, restore or remove the missing image, and supply correctly sized responsive sources.

findings.summary: Chrome reports platform hygiene issues
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed deprecations and inspector-issues audits and reported legacy JavaScript savings of 40 KiB.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve DevTools Issues and deprecation warnings, then serve a modern bundle without avoidable legacy transforms to Baseline browsers.

findings.summary: HTTPS is strong, but essential response defenses are absent
findings.evidence: Header inspection confirms HTTPS and two-year preload HSTS, but no Content-Security-Policy and no X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP with frame-ancestors and add X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff; roll out CSP in report-only mode first.

findings.summary: The default page has an unusually broad tracking footprint
findings.evidence: Tracker capture found 35 third-party origins and ten known tracker domains. HAR recorded 72 third-party requests and 2.53 MB third-party transfer, including advertising and Amplitude session replay.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise vendors, disable session replay by default, gate non-essential analytics on consent, and batch the remaining privacy-preserving measurements.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced policy coverage is incomplete and analytics cookies are weakly scoped
findings.evidence: Headers lacked clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy. Cookie audit found 13 of 14 cookies without Secure and several SameSite=None analytics cookies lasting 365-400 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Add frame-ancestors, strict Referrer-Policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy; mark all HTTPS cookies Secure, avoid SameSite=None unless required, and shorten analytics retention.

findings.summary: Consent offers Accept but no equally direct Reject action
findings.evidence: The initial consent panel foregrounds Accept and Advanced Settings while claiming processing by 1,192 vendors; rejecting non-essential processing requires a deeper flow.
findings.suggestedFix: Place Reject non-essential beside Accept with equal prominence, use privacy-preserving defaults, and keep granular settings optional.

findings.summary: Landing imagery is not delivered responsively or in modern formats
findings.evidence: Image audit found 64 legacy-format images, 61 without srcset, 26 below-fold images loaded eagerly, and one oversized image. Lighthouse estimated 431 KiB image-delivery savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants and width-based srcset/sizes, preserve dimensions, and lazy-load all below-fold cards.

findings.summary: Advertising and analytics perform substantial work before the user asks for it
findings.evidence: The initial HAR transfers 2.53 MB from third parties and the trace/Lighthouse show heavy scripting before interaction, including ad bidding and session replay.
findings.suggestedFix: Deprioritise or conditionally import background dependencies after consent and idle; stop replay and ad work when the page is hidden.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts dominate the page budget
findings.evidence: Of 3.51 MB transferred, 2.53 MB came from third parties; the largest files include ad, tag-manager, bidder, consent, and session-replay scripts rather than core esports content.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, remove low-value vendors, self-host only justified dependencies, and cache/defer the remainder.

findings.summary: High-value public content is intentionally unavailable to major AI agents
findings.evidence: robots.txt blocks GPTBot, ClaudeBot, ChatGPT-User, Amazonbot, meta-externalagent and others from all paths, while discoverability captures show 73-90% of representative content is available in raw HTML. No WebMCP capability surface was detected.
findings.suggestedFix: Choose and publish an explicit agent access policy. Where safe, permit retrieval of public reference pages and expose bounded read/search capabilities with structured inputs and outputs.
